title_en: Regulations on Customs Protection of Intellectual Property Rights of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of implementing customs protection of intellectual property rights, promoting foreign economic trade and scientific, technological and cultural exchanges, and safeguarding public interests.

Article 2 For the purposes of these Regulations, "customs protection of intellectual property rights" means the protection implemented by the Customs against the exclusive right to use a trademark, copyright and rights related to copyright, and patent right (hereinafter collectively referred to as "intellectual property rights") that are related to imported or exported goods and are protected by the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 The State prohibits the import or export of goods that infringe intellectual property rights.
The Customs shall, in accordance with the relevant laws and the provisions of these Regulations, implement protection of intellectual property rights and exercise the relevant powers provided for in the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 4 Where an intellectual property right holder requests the Customs to implement protection of intellectual property rights, he shall submit an application to the Customs for adopting protection measures.

Article 5 The consignee or its agent of imported goods, and the consignor or its agent of exported goods shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, truthfully declare to the Customs the status of intellectual property rights related to the imported or exported goods, and submit relevant certifying documents.
Article 6 When implementing protection of intellectual property rights, the Customs shall keep confidential the trade secrets of the relevant parties.

Article 9 Where the Customs discovers that an intellectual property right holder, when applying for the recordal of intellectual property rights, has failed to truthfully provide relevant information or documents, the General Administration of Customs may revoke the recordal.

Article 10 The recordal of customs protection of intellectual property rights shall take effect from the date of approval by the General Administration of Customs, and shall be valid for a term of 10 years.
If the intellectual property right is still valid, the intellectual property right holder may, within 6 months prior to the expiry of the validity term of the recordal of customs protection of intellectual property rights, apply to the General Administration of Customs for renewal of the recordal. The validity term of each renewal shall be 10 years.
If the validity term of the recordal of customs protection of intellectual property rights expires and no application for renewal is made, or if the intellectual property right is no longer protected by laws or administrative regulations, the recordal of customs protection of intellectual property rights shall immediately cease to have effect.

Article 11 Where the recordal information of intellectual property rights changes, the intellectual property right holder shall, within 30 working days from the date of change, go through the formalities for modification or cancellation of the recordal with the General Administration of Customs.
If the intellectual property right holder fails to go through the modification or cancellation formalities in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, thereby causing serious impact on the lawful import or export of goods by others or on the Customs' performance of its supervision duties according to law, the General Administration of Customs may, upon application by an interested party, revoke the relevant recordal, or may revoke the relevant recordal on its own initiative.

Article 12 Where an intellectual property right holder discovers that goods suspected of infringing an intellectual property right are about to be imported or exported, he may submit an application to the Customs at the place of entry or exit for detaining the goods suspected of infringement.

Article 14 Where an intellectual property right holder requests the Customs to detain goods suspected of infringement, he shall provide the Customs with a guarantee not exceeding the equivalent value of the goods, to be used for compensating the loss that may be caused to the consignee or consignor due to an improper application, and for paying the costs of storage, custody and disposal of the goods after detention by the Customs; if the intellectual property right holder directly pays the storage and custody costs to the warehouseman, such costs shall be deducted from the guarantee. The specific measures shall be formulated by the General Administration of Customs.

Article 15 Where an intellectual property right holder applies for detention of goods suspected of infringement, satisfies the provisions of Article 13 of these Regulations, and provides a guarantee in accordance with Article 14 of these Regulations, the Customs shall detain the goods suspected of infringement, notify the intellectual property right holder in writing, and serve the Customs detention receipt on the consignee or consignor.
Where an intellectual property right holder applies for detention of goods suspected of infringement, but fails to satisfy the provisions of Article 13 of these Regulations, or fails to provide a guarantee in accordance with Article 14 of these Regulations, the Customs shall reject the application and notify the intellectual property right holder in writing.

Article 16 Where the Customs discovers that imported or exported goods are suspected of infringing a recorded intellectual property right, it shall immediately notify the intellectual property right holder in writing. If the intellectual property right holder, within 3 working days from the date of service of the notice, submits an application in accordance with Article 13 of these Regulations and provides a guarantee in accordance with Article 14 of these Regulations, the Customs shall detain the goods suspected of infringement, notify the intellectual property right holder in writing, and serve the Customs detention receipt on the consignee or consignor. If the intellectual property right holder fails to submit an application or provide a guarantee within the prescribed time limit, the Customs shall not detain the goods.
Article 17 With the consent of the Customs, the intellectual property right holder and the consignee or consignor may inspect the relevant goods.

Article 18 Where the consignee or consignor believes that its goods do not infringe the intellectual property rights of the intellectual property right holder, it shall submit a written explanation to the Customs and attach relevant evidence.

Article 19 Where the consignee or consignor of goods suspected of infringing a patent right believes that its imported or exported goods do not infringe the patent right, it may, after providing a bond equivalent to the value of the goods to the Customs, request the Customs to release the goods. If the intellectual property right holder fails to bring a prosecution in the People's Court within a reasonable period, the Customs shall refund the bond.

Article 20 Where, after the Customs discovers that imported or exported goods are suspected of infringing a recorded intellectual property right and notifies the intellectual property right holder, the intellectual property right holder requests the Customs to detain the goods suspected of infringement, the Customs shall, within 30 working days from the date of detention, investigate and determine whether the detained goods suspected of infringement infringe the intellectual property right; if it cannot make a determination, it shall immediately notify the intellectual property right holder in writing.

Article 21 Where the Customs investigates the suspected infringing goods detained and requests the competent intellectual property department to provide assistance, the relevant competent intellectual property department shall provide such assistance.
Where the competent intellectual property department handles an infringement case involving imported or exported goods and requests the Customs to provide assistance, the Customs shall provide such assistance.
Article 22 When the Customs investigates the detained suspected infringing goods and the relevant circumstances, the intellectual property right holder and the consignee or consignor shall cooperate.

Article 23 After filing an application with the Customs for taking protective measures, the intellectual property right holder may, in accordance with the provisions of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China or other relevant laws, apply to the People's Court for an order to cease the infringing act or for property preservation measures with respect to the detained suspected infringing goods.
Where the Customs receives a notice from the People's Court for assistance in enforcement of an order to cease the infringing act or property preservation, it shall provide assistance.

Article 25 Where the Customs detains suspected infringing goods in accordance with these Regulations, the intellectual property right holder shall pay the relevant expenses for storage, custody, and disposal, among others. If the intellectual property right holder fails to pay the relevant expenses, the Customs may deduct them from the security deposit provided by the intellectual property right holder to the Customs, or require the guarantor to perform the relevant guarantee obligations.
Where the suspected infringing goods are determined to infringe intellectual property rights, the intellectual property right holder may include the relevant expenses for storage, custody, and disposal, among others, paid by it into the reasonable expenses incurred for stopping the infringing act.

Article 26 Where the Customs, in implementing intellectual property protection, discovers a case suspected of constituting a crime, it shall transfer the case to the public security organ for handling according to law.

Article 27 Where the detained suspected infringing goods are determined to infringe intellectual property rights after investigation by the Customs, the Customs shall confiscate them.
After confiscating goods that infringe intellectual property rights, the Customs shall notify the intellectual property right holder in writing of the relevant information concerning the goods.
If the confiscated goods that infringe intellectual property rights can be used for social welfare undertakings, the Customs shall transfer them to relevant welfare institutions for use in social welfare undertakings; if the intellectual property right holder is willing to purchase them, the Customs may transfer them to the intellectual property right holder for a price. If the confiscated goods that infringe intellectual property rights cannot be used for social welfare undertakings and the intellectual property right holder is not willing to purchase them, the Customs may auction them according to law after eliminating the infringing features; however, for imported goods bearing counterfeit trademarks, except under special circumstances, they may not be allowed to enter commercial channels merely by removing the trademark identifiers from the goods; if the infringing features cannot be eliminated, the Customs shall destroy them.

Article 28 After the Customs accepts the recordal of intellectual property protection and the application for taking protective measures, if the Customs fails to discover infringing goods, fails to take protective measures in a timely manner, or fails to take effective protective measures due to the intellectual property right holder's failure to provide accurate information, the intellectual property right holder shall bear the responsibility itself.
Where, after the intellectual property right holder requests the Customs to detain suspected infringing goods, the Customs cannot determine that the detained suspected infringing goods infringe the intellectual property rights of the intellectual property right holder, or the People's Court renders a judgment that the goods do not infringe the intellectual property rights of the intellectual property right holder, the intellectual property right holder shall bear compensation liability according to law.
Article 29 Where the import or export of goods that infringe intellectual property rights constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 30 Where a Customs staff member, in implementing intellectual property protection, neglects duty, abuses power, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, and if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if the act does not constitute a crime, an administrative sanction shall be imposed according to law.

Article 31 Where articles carried or mailed by an individual into or out of the territory exceed the reasonable quantity for personal use and infringe the intellectual property rights specified in Article 2 of these Regulations, they shall be treated as infringing goods.

Article 32 These Regulations shall come into force as of March 1, 2004. The Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Customs Protection of Intellectual Property Rights promulgated by the State Council on July 5, 1995 shall be abolished simultaneously.
